question: A programme manager has a Claude-drafted quarterly performance report and one hour to review it before it goes to her director. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) List what the original request asked the report to cover; check the draft against that list for anything missing; verify the claims and figures that carry the most weight; note what was checked and pass the draft to the director.

B) List what the original request asked the report to cover; verify the claims and figures that carry the most weight; note what was checked and pass the draft to the director; check the draft against that list for anything missing.

C) Verify the claims and figures that carry the most weight; check the draft against that list for anything missing; list what the original request asked the report to cover; note what was checked and pass the draft to the director.

D) Check the draft against that list for anything missing; list what the original request asked the report to cover; verify the claims and figures that carry the most weight; note what was checked and pass the draft to the director.
correct_answers: A) List what the original request asked the report to cover; check the draft against that list for anything missing; verify the claims and figures that carry the most weight; note what was checked and pass the draft to the director.
explanations: Correct. Restating what was asked for gives her a standard; comparing the draft against it exposes missing sections cheaply and tells her where the substance actually is; verification effort then goes to the claims that matter most; recording what was checked lets the director see the limits of the review.
The draft reaches the director before the completeness check, so a missing section is discovered only after the report has already been handed over.
Verification begins before anyone has established what the report was meant to contain, so the hour is spent on whatever happens to be on the page and the coverage list arrives too late to direct it.
The draft is compared against a list that has not been written yet, so the comparison has no standard behind it and reduces to reading the report and hoping something looks absent.
